title: Repair unfair backlog amplification for heterogeneous short/long-context mixes causing tail latency spikes
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Summary: Production escalations from two paying customers surfaced a recurring pattern: when a mixed workload (short, interactive requests interleaved with long-context generation jobs) runs against Redwood's continuous batching scheduler, short requests experience sustained tail latency spikes and dropped SLAs. Impact spans Hosted, Dedicated, and some Private deployments where autoscaling or tenant isolation is configured differently.

Symptoms observed: 
- Short requests (<=64 tokens) that previously had p99 < 120ms spiked to 800ms+ intermittently during sustained long-context bursts.
- Queue depth metrics show long requests occupying multiple batch slots for extended time, causing head-of-line effects and backlog amplification.
- KV cache churn increases as long requests trigger larger KV cache allocations/evictions, slowing small-request fast-paths.
- In Dedicated pools with reserved capacity, autoscaler oscillation leaves insufficient pre-warmed slots for low-latency flows.

Root cause hypothesis and confirmation: 
- The continuous batching scheduler's adaptive floodgate threshold uses aggregate token rate and average batch fill heuristics; it fails to account for heterogeneity in request length distributions. Long requests cause batch formation to favor throughput (fewer, larger batches) while starving short latency-sensitive flows. We confirmed via replayed production traces that the scheduler's batch window and per-tenant token accounting allowed a small number of long requests to consume a disproportionate fraction of dispatch budget.
- KV cache eviction policy exposed a secondary effect: when long requests bring in large KV slices, eviction thrashes the cache used by short-path inference, increasing memory pressure and kernel warmups.

Fix implemented (hotfix + planned follow-ups): 
1) Hotfix (deployed 2026-03-03): introduce a per-tenant "latency token budget" that reserves a small fraction of dispatch capacity for latency-sensitive requests. This prevents full preemption by long requests and unblocks short flows quickly. Implemented as a lightweight amendment in dispatcher with an emergency fallback to old behavior if metrics degrade.
2) Scheduler improvement (in progress): change batch admission to a weighted fairness policy — short requests get higher effective weight within mixed batches; also cap per-request max batch-hold time for requests flagged as low-latency.
3) KV cache tweaks (in review): add size-based admission to KV cache for long contexts to avoid eviction storms; small-request fast-path uses a protected cache slice.
4) Autoscaler policy changes for Dedicated pools (planning): add predictive warmup for short-request load and hysteresis on scale-down to avoid losing warm capacity during mixed bursts.

Rollout plan: 
- Hotfix rolled to Hosted first (canary 5% traffic on 2026-03-03, 25% 2026-03-04, full ramp 2026-03-05).
- Dedicated customers: coordinated patch with SRE and account teams; scheduled maintenance window for two affected customers (2026-03-06 and 2026-03-08).
- Private deployments: publish optional patch notes + migration guide; for air-gapped customers provide patch bundle.

Observability and tests added: 
- New per-tenant "token budget exhaustion" gauge and alert in Grafana; synthetic canary test for mixed short/long trace injected every 5m.
- Extended integration tests in CI that replay production request mixes (short/long ratios) and assert p50/p95/p99 stabilities.
- Postmortem runbook updated with mitigation steps and a checklist for contacting customers.

Customer communication: 
- Incident emails and mitigation notes sent to affected customers (AcmeDocs and FinSight) with temporary workarounds (limit long-context jobs or route them to dedicated background queues).
- Customer success scheduled follow-ups and SLAs adjustments where appropriate.

Outstanding work and follow-ups (owners): 
- Finalize weighted fairness algorithm and land in runtime-1.21 (owner: Diego Alvarez).
- Load-test the KV cache protected slice at scale and iterate (owner: Priya Rao).
- Autoscaler predictive warmup POC and Dedicated playbook (owner: Marco Santoro).

2026-03-08 - SRE (review): Noted autoscaler oscillation still present for one Dedicated pool when background long-job backlog spikes. Added follow-up ENG-31058 to prototype scale-down hysteresis.
